Create a study project with `uv`, then add SCGSim `3.0.0rc4` and the OrcaPen SC PDK, the component library every example imports. SCGSim supports Python `>=3.12,<3.14`.

## 1. Install uv and Git

Install [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) and [Git](https://git-scm.com/downloads). Git lets `uv` fetch SCGSim from the [canonical source repository](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/scgsim).

Check: `uv --version` and `git --version` each print an installed version.

## 2. Create the project and add SCGSim

Initialize a project with Python 3.12 and add SCGSim and the PDK. These are the commands of the [home page](../../index.qmd#install): SCGSim at the tag `v3.0.0rc4` with its `aedt` extra, and the PDK at the revision the examples use.

```bash
uv init --python 3.12 scgsim-study
cd scgsim-study
uv add 'scgsim[aedt] @ git+https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/scgsim.git@v3.0.0rc4' \
  'orcapen-sc-pdk @ git+https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/orcapen-sc-pdk.git@49e539fd59f3224ecda965d777c7ec3aadcc3b85'
```

`uv.lock` records the exact Git revision of each dependency.

## 3. Check the installation

Run a Python import and print the installed package version:

```bash
uv run python -c 'import scgsim; from importlib.metadata import version; print(version("scgsim"))'
```

Check: the command prints the installed SCGSim version without an import error.

## Add a backend extra

The base package reads returned results; the command above adds the `aedt` extra. To prepare Palace runs, add the `palace` extra to the existing SCGSim dependency:

```bash
uv add --extra palace scgsim
```

Use `aedt-epr` or `visualization` the same way when you need those features. The extra is added to the existing Git dependency and keeps its configured source. `aedt` and `aedt-epr` include OCP (`cadquery-ocp-novtk`), the geometry kernel that writes the STEP file AEDT imports.

## Rebuild the environment on another computer

Keep `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` with the study. On another computer, run `uv sync` in the project directory to recreate the locked environment:

```bash
uv sync
```
